categoryRules: Categories describe how a recipe is served. Choose one primary category, with a second only when clearly useful. Do not classify every main course as Lunch and Dinner; those occasions are deliberately omitted. Empty lists are allowed when nothing fits. Maximum two categories. Every selected category needs positive source support; never add a second category to fill the array. A chicken curry is not Desserts or Cakes & baking. Source validation patterns are conservative evidence gates, not a complete classifier.

tagRules: Choose every clearly supported tag that adds useful filtering information, generally no more than eight. This is a relevance target, not a reason to discard a clearly applicable tag. Never invent a tag or infer attributes from the title alone when ingredients or instructions contradict them.

dietaryValidation.reason: Meat, fish, seafood or other non-vegetarian ingredient evidence
Egg, dairy, honey or other non-vegan ingredient evidence

tagGroups.rules: Use only when the source identifies the cuisine or the recipe has a clear, specific culinary identity. An ingredient alone (such as soy sauce) is insufficient. Omit cuisine when uncertain; this starter list can grow with the collection. The first evidence-rule pass auto-selects cuisine only from explicit introduction wording; culinary-identity inferences remain review suggestions.
These work across serving categories: a soup can be a starter or a main course, for example.
Apply when the ingredient is central to the dish, not a garnish, stock or minor seasoning. Several may apply. Seafood means shellfish and other seafood apart from finfish, which uses Fish.

Check EVERY ingredient, including stocks, sauces, garnishes and optional ingredients, before selecting dietary tags. Vegetarian excludes meat, poultry, fish, seafood, meat stocks, fish sauce, gelatine and animal-rennet cheese. Vegan additionally excludes dairy, eggs, honey and other animal-derived ingredients. Chicken, Turkey, Beef, Pork, Lamb, Fish or Seafood tags must NEVER coexist with Vegetarian or Vegan; Eggs must NEVER coexist with Vegan. A chicken curry with vegetables is neither Vegetarian nor Vegan. A recipe with eggs or dairy may be Vegetarian but is not Vegan. Use the recipe as written, not a possible adaptation: optional meat or a suggested plant-based substitution does not qualify the whole recipe. Apply both Vegetarian and Vegan to vegan recipes so vegetarian filtering also finds them. Withhold these tags if an ambiguous ingredient could change the classification, unless the source specifies a suitable version. Do not silently substitute ingredients to qualify a recipe. Allergen-free, gluten-free and medical-diet tags are deliberately outside this initial list; ordinary recipe text often lacks the product details needed to establish them reliably.

Apply only when the recipe actually uses the method. A tool tag is useful for filtering even though the same appliance may also appear under Required tools. One pot means one cooking vessel; a mixing bowl does not disqualify it. No cook means no heat is required anywhere in the method. Use Traybake from Dish type for food cooked together on a baking tray.

Quick requires a known or explicitly estimated total elapsed time of at most 30 minutes, including waits. Make ahead requires source guidance on preparing in advance. Freezer friendly requires explicit source freezing guidance; do not guess storage suitability or invent storage instructions.

sourceValidation.label: Make ahead
sourceValidation.sourcePattern: (?im)^\s*(?:\d+[.)]\s*)?(?:make ahead\s*:|(?:you can |to |this (?:dish|recipe) can be )?(?:prepare|make|cook|assemble)[^.!?\r\n]{0,80}\b(?:in advance|ahead|the day before)\b)

evidenceRules.policy: Evaluate all approved labels against scoped source evidence. Supporting ingredients do not establish a main ingredient tag. Preselect every approved model tag and local tag suggestion. Keep evidence conflicts visible for manual correction. Estimated qualifying totals suggest Quick. Cuisine requires explicit wording in recipe introduction. Manual overrides are preserved on recheck.

tagDefinitions.name: Soup
tagDefinitions.description: Select Soup when the finished dish is a soup served with a liquid or blended base. Stock used inside another dish does not qualify.

tagDefinitions.name: Stew
tagDefinitions.description: Select Stew for a simmered dish of substantial pieces in gravy or sauce, served as a stew.

tagDefinitions.name: Curry
tagDefinitions.description: Select Curry when the recipe makes a curry. Curry powder used as seasoning in another dish is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Salad
tagDefinitions.description: Select Salad when the finished dish is a salad, including substantial cooked or grain salads. A side salad mentioned for serving is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Pasta
tagDefinitions.description: Select Pasta when pasta is a central part of the finished dish, including pasta bakes and lasagne.

tagDefinitions.name: Noodles
tagDefinitions.description: Select Noodles when noodles are central to the dish. A suggested noodle accompaniment alone is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Rice dish
tagDefinitions.description: Select Rice dish when rice is central to the recipe, such as risotto, paella or a rice bowl. Rice mentioned only as a serving suggestion is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Pizza
tagDefinitions.description: Select Pizza for pizza or a pizza-style assembled dish. Pizza sauce by itself does not qualify.

tagDefinitions.name: Pie & tart
tagDefinitions.description: Select Pie & tart for pies or tarts, including pastry pies and potato-topped shepherd's or cottage pies. Pastry alone is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Sandwich & wrap
tagDefinitions.description: Select Sandwich & wrap for filled sandwiches, wraps, burritos or similar handheld assembled dishes. A deconstructed bowl alone does not qualify.

tagDefinitions.name: Traybake
tagDefinitions.description: Select Traybake when the dish cooks together on a baking tray. Simply putting one component on a tray is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Chicken
tagDefinitions.description: Select Chicken when chicken meat is central. Chicken stock, flavouring or garnish alone is insufficient. Plant-based chicken alternatives do not qualify.

tagDefinitions.name: Turkey
tagDefinitions.description: Select Turkey when turkey meat is central. Turkey stock, flavouring or garnish alone is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Beef
tagDefinitions.description: Select Beef when beef or veal meat is central. Beef stock, gravy or flavouring alone is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Pork
tagDefinitions.description: Select Pork when pork, bacon, ham or another pork product is central. A small garnish or seasoning alone is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Lamb
tagDefinitions.description: Select Lamb when lamb or mutton meat is central. Lamb stock or flavouring alone is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Fish
tagDefinitions.description: Select Fish when finfish such as salmon, tuna or cod is central. Fish stock, fish sauce or a minor anchovy seasoning alone is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Seafood
tagDefinitions.description: Select Seafood when shellfish or other non-finfish seafood is central, such as prawns, crab, mussels or squid. Finfish uses Fish.

tagDefinitions.name: Eggs
tagDefinitions.description: Select Eggs when eggs are central, such as an omelette, frittata or egg salad. Glazing pastry or binding a mixture with an egg alone is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Beans & lentils
tagDefinitions.description: Select Beans & lentils when legumes such as beans, lentils or chickpeas are central. Coffee beans and vanilla beans do not qualify.

tagDefinitions.name: Tofu & tempeh
tagDefinitions.description: Select Tofu & tempeh when tofu or tempeh is central to the finished dish.

tagDefinitions.name: Vegetables
tagDefinitions.description: Select Vegetables when vegetables are central to the finished dish. A little onion, garnish or seasoning in a meat dish is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Vegetarian
tagDefinitions.description: Select Vegetarian only when every ingredient, including optional additions, stocks and sauces, is vegetarian. Exclude meat, fish, seafood, gelatine, animal fats and animal-rennet cheese. Withhold when compound ingredients are ambiguous.

tagDefinitions.name: Vegan
tagDefinitions.description: Select Vegan only when every ingredient, including optional additions, stocks and sauces, is plant-based. Exclude meat, fish, eggs, dairy, honey and other animal products. Withhold ambiguous compounds. Vegan recipes also qualify as Vegetarian.

tagDefinitions.name: One pot
tagDefinitions.description: Select One pot when the whole recipe uses one cooking vessel. Mixing bowls do not disqualify it, but separately cooking rice or pasta in another pan does.

tagDefinitions.name: Air fryer
tagDefinitions.description: Select Air fryer when the method actually cooks food in an air fryer. Equipment lists or statements saying not to use one are insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Slow cooker
tagDefinitions.description: Select Slow cooker when the method actually uses a slow cooker. Long cooking in an oven or an unused equipment mention is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Pressure cooker
tagDefinitions.description: Select Pressure cooker when the method pressure-cooks food in a pressure cooker or pressure setting. An unused appliance mention is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: Barbecue
tagDefinitions.description: Select Barbecue when the method cooks on a barbecue or BBQ. Barbecue sauce or an unused equipment mention is insufficient.

tagDefinitions.name: No cook
tagDefinitions.description: Select No cook only when no heating is required anywhere in the recipe. Boiling water, melting ingredients or cooking a component disqualifies it.

tagDefinitions.name: Quick (30 minutes or less)
tagDefinitions.description: Select Quick (30 minutes or less) when total elapsed preparation-to-serving time is at most 30 minutes, including resting, chilling and other waits. Use total time rather than hands-on time.

tagDefinitions.name: Make ahead
tagDefinitions.description: Select Make ahead when the source explicitly describes preparing the dish or a component in advance. Meal-prep guidance qualifies; a slow cooking method by itself does not.

tagDefinitions.name: Freezer friendly
tagDefinitions.description: Select Freezer friendly when the source explicitly calls the recipe freezable or gives affirmative freezing guidance. Do not infer this from ingredients or from negated instructions.
